sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 5:41

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 5:41:1
items.html: Lo Mati in Keter, etc.: For the coarseness of phase three of the female and of phase four of the male in the vessel of Keter refined once more, and then the ZON of Keter departed to its root, and then it turned its face downward, that is, it annulled its face, and the posterior became the face, as above. And then it gave the remainder in it, which is the coarseness of phase three of the male and phase two of the female, to the vessel of Hochma. And then it is Mati in Hochma.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 5:41:2
items.html: And then Bina should have remained there in Hochma as at first. For after the face returned to its place in Hochma, HB immediately return to a single degree, so that Bina is in the vessel of Hochma, as above. However, here it did not remain so, for Hochma turned her face downward and her posterior upward and returned the ZON of Bina to the vessel of Bina, and they were divided once again into two Partzufim. And understand this well. For at first, when the vessel of Hochma received her lights, the ZON, and the face of Hochma returned to its place as at the beginning, then certainly Bina and Hochma joined and became a single vessel, for the above reason given at the birth of the Gadlut of Hesed, study it there well. For so it is here too: since Hesed is in the vessel of Bina, which has joined with the vessel of Hochma, it again receives the illumination of Hochma as at first, and Hesed is once more found to have grown and not to need its mother. But it still cannot descend of itself into its own vessel except through the bestowal of Bina. Therefore Hochma had to return the ZON of Bina to the vessel of Bina, for then Bina, too, turns her face downward and returns the light of Hesed to its place, to its own vessel.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 5:41:3
items.html: But because of the light of Hesed that is in her place, she therefore descends to be there with him. That is, that had Bina remained joined in the vessel of Hochma, Hesed would have remained in her place and would not have descended to its own vessel of Hesed, as above in the adjacent item, and study it there.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 5:41:4
items.html: For He delights in Hesed. For this is the whole nature of Bina: that she craves Hassadim more than the light of Hochma. And this is what caused the refinement of the coarseness of phase three of the male of Hochma to phase two, and after this of phase two of Bina to phase one, whose light is the light of Hassadim. And then she is found face to face with the vessel of Hesed, and then she gives the light of Hesed back to the vessel of Hesed, as above at length. And this is what he says, “when Bina descended to her place, then Hesed does not need her, and it descends to its place.” For after it has already received the illumination of Hochma, from the time when the vessel of Bina and the vessel of Hochma were joined together, as above, it no longer needs the nursing of the vessel of Bina, and therefore it descends to its place.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 5:41:5
items.html:
Lo Mati in Gevura, and then the vessel of Gevura turns her face downward. For the whole division of Gevura from Hesed came about because of the two distances, that is, because of the return of the ZON of Keter to their place, whose posterior detained the light of Hochma from the vessel of Hochma; and then the illumination of Hochma to Hesed was cut off, and it therefore turned its face downward and gave the aspect of VAK to Gevura, as above. Therefore, now that Hesed has again attained its GAR, it follows of itself that the aspect of the light of Gevura, which had separated from the GAR, returned once more to the vessel of Hesed as at first, before they were separated.
And see and understand that the matter is entirely like the ways of the vessels of Hochma and Bina above. For just as the division of the lights of the ZON of Hochma and the ZON of Bina came about by reason of the turning of the posterior of the vessel of Hochma — which means that Hochma abandoned the bestowal of her GAR and bestowed only VAK, which are the aspect of the ZON of the vessel of Bina — so too the lights of Hesed and Gevura were divided by the force of the turning of the face of the vessel of Hesed: after the illumination of GAR was withheld from it by the force of the two distances, it turned its face and bestowed VAK without GAR, which is the light of Gevura, as above. And just as, after Lo Mati in Keter, the force of its posterior was annulled and it returned the light of Hochma to the vessel of Hochma, whereupon the face of Hochma returned to its place as at first, and thereby the lights of the ZON of Hochma and of the ZON of Bina were united once more into a single Partzuf, as above — the same holds here also. For after Hesed attained the illumination of Hochma, from the time of its being in the vessel of Bina during her union with Hochma, as above, and returned with the Gadlut to its place, whereupon its face returned as at first, the lights of Hesed and Gevura are found to be united into a single light. And all this is because the light is not divided into GAR and VAK except by reason of some cause that compels it to this; therefore, the very moment the cause is annulled, they return to being a single light as at first.
And this is what he says, “Lo Mati in Gevura, and then the vessel of Gevura turns her face downward and gives the five lights downward, in Tifferet.” For when the light of Gevura joins with the light of Hesed into one, this joining acts upon their vessels as well; and since the vessel of Gevura joined with the vessel of Hesed, she thereby turned her face downward, for she annulled her face, which had detained the bestowal of GAR, and turned her posterior upward, that is, she turned to bestow the illumination of GAR like the vessel of Hesed. And then she bestowed her remainder, which belongs to Tifferet, to the vessel of Tifferet, and Tifferet, too, receives the illumination of GAR. And this is the secret of Tifferet being called a Vav [ו] with a head, whose meaning is that same illumination of GAR that it receives through the bestowal of the light of Gevura, at the time when Gevura is joined as one with the light of Hesed. And with this you will understand what is brought in several places, that Tifferet is blended of Hesed and Gevura together — namely as above, that it receives the remainder of the light of Gevura from the time of its being joined as one with the light of Hesed. And understand this.
Now the Sefira of Tifferet of ZA is understood by us from its source. For its vessel is the aspect of Bina of the VAK, since the HGT are the KHB of the VAK, as above. Yet it is discerned only as the aspect of the Sefira of Daat of the VAK, and this is by reason of its light, which is the aspect of Daat. But first we must know what the light of Daat is, for we have only ten Sefirot — KHB, HGT, NHYM — and it is known what is written in Sefer Yetzira, “ten and not eleven.” If so, what is this light of Daat? And know that the source of this light is in the exchange of the lights in the second expansion that is here. For here the light of Hochma came to the vessel of Keter, and the light of Bina to the vessel of Hochma, and the light of Hesed to the vessel of Bina, and the light of Malchut to the vessel of ZA, and the vessel of Malchut remained without light, as is known from the words of the ARI. And this light of Hesed that came to the vessel of Bina is the source of the light of Daat; and this is why the ARI calls it by the name of the son of Bina, and its aspect of Aba and Ima are the male and the female in the vessel of Bina — in such a way that the male is the aspect of Hochma of the vessel of Bina, and the female is the aspect of Bina of the vessel of Bina, and the light of Hesed is the aspect of the Daat between this HB, which is always called the aspect of the son of HB. And more precisely: the ZON of the vessel of Hochma, both of them together, are considered the aspect of Hochma and the aspect of Aba; and the ZON that are in the vessel of Bina, both of them together, are considered the aspect of Bina and the aspect of Ima; and the light of Hesed that is in the vessel of Bina is considered the aspect of Daat and the aspect of the son of that Aba and Ima. And with this it is understood that the light of Hesed was emanated at its beginning from the remainder of the light of the ZON of Hochma, after they refined to phase one, and came to the vessel of Bina, which is its Ima; and there, in the womb of the vessel of Bina, it tarried until it attained the illumination of Hochma, that is, until it grew, and then it emerged into the place of the vessels of the VAK, which are called the air of the world. And this is not the place to elaborate.
And so the light of Daat has been explained to us from its root: that it is a son and an offspring, newly formed by reason of the exchange of the lights in the second expansion. For this is why it came and clothed in the vessel of Bina, even though it is only the light of ZA and the aspect of VAK, which has no comparison whatever to the aspect of GAR — for the difference between the GAR and the VAK is as far as the difference between a light and its vessel. And even so, by reason of the exchange of the lights, this light of VAK came and clothed in a vessel of GAR; and this is a very wondrous matter. Contemplate this, for this is not the place to elaborate on what is not needed for our subject.
And from all that has been explained until here you will understand that these three Sefirot, HGT of ZA, are not considered the substance of ZA itself, but the aspect of the GAR — KHB, or HBD — of ZA, as above. Of the five ends, HGT NH, they are exactly the five phases KHB, ZA and Malchut, only that when they are the aspect of the light of Hassadim and the light of VAK, their names are changed to HGT NH. And so the substance of the aspect of ZA begins from the fourth end of the five Hassadim, which is called Netzah, since it stands opposite the fourth phase, which is called ZA; whereas Tifferet stands opposite the third phase, which is called Bina. And remember this.
And therefore the lights of HGT, too, are the aspect of GAR, except that they begin from Hochma, for the above reason. And the light of Hesed is discerned as the light of Hochma of the VAK, and the light of Gevura is discerned as the light of Bina of the VAK, as above; and the light of Tifferet is discerned as that same light of Hesed from the side of its clothing in the vessel of Bina, that is, the aspect of the light of Daat and the son of HB, which is the very substance of the light of the VAK. This is not so with the lights of Hesed and Gevura, which are considered the aspect of the illuminations of Hochma and Bina that reached this light of Hesed, but are not the essence of the light of Hesed from the aspect of its own being.
And the reason is from the side of the relation of the vessels. For since Hesed and Gevura are, from their source, in the aspect of the vessels of Keter and Hochma, as above, and since this light of Hesed never clothed in these vessels, it therefore does not clothe in the vessels of Hesed and Gevura either. But since it did clothe in the vessel of Bina, its place is therefore found among the vessels of the VAK in the vessel of Tifferet, which is in the place of Bina, as above. And therefore Tifferet is considered the chief aspect of the Partzuf of ZA, and the body of the tree; and the essence of the above light of Hesed within it is considered the watering of the tree; and all the remaining Sefirot of the seven lower ones are considered its branches, which hang upon it, upon Tifferet.
